questions.q: When did Solomon begin building the temple of Yahweh?
questions.a: Solomon began building the temple of Yahweh in the 480th year after the people of Israel came out of Egypt.

questions.q: What were the dimensions of the temple that Solomon built for Yahweh?
questions.a: The temple that Solomon built was 60 cubits long, 20 cubits wide, and 30 cubits high.

questions.q: Did Solomon make windows for the house?
questions.a: Yes, Solomon made framed windows for the house.

questions.q: Where were the stones for the house prepared?
questions.a: The stones for the house were prepared at the quarry.

questions.q: What did Solomon use to cover the house?
questions.a: Solomon covered the house with beams and boards of cedar.

questions.q: How were the side rooms joined to the house?
questions.a: The side rooms were joined to the house with beams of cedar.

questions.q: Did Yahweh promise to live among the people of Israel?
questions.a: Yes, Yahweh promised to live among the people of Israel and to never abandon them.

questions.q: What did Solomon use to build the interior walls of the house?
questions.a: Solomon used boards of cedar to build the interior walls of the house.

questions.q: What was the length of the main hall of the house?
questions.a: The main hall of the house was 40 cubits long.

questions.q: Why did Solomon prepare the inner sanctuary inside the house?
questions.a: Solomon prepared the inner sanctuary inside the house in order to place the Box of the Covenant of Yahweh there.

questions.q: What did Solomon use to overlay the inside of the temple and the altar of the inner sanctuary?
questions.a: Solomon overlaid the entire interior of the temple and the altar of the inner sanctuary with gold.

questions.q: What was the height of the cherubim that Solomon made for the most holy place?
questions.a: Solomon made the two cherubim for the most holy place ten cubits high.

questions.q: Where did Solomon place the cherubim he had made?
questions.a: Solomon placed the cherubim in the midst of the inner house.

questions.q: What did Solomon carve on the walls of the house?
questions.a: Solomon carved figures of cherubim, palm trees, and open flowers on the walls of the house.

questions.q: Did Solomon make doors for the entrance to the inner sanctuary?
questions.a: Yes, Solomon made doors of olive wood for the entrance to the inner sanctuary.

questions.q: How long did Solomon take to build the temple?
questions.a: Solomon took seven years to build the temple.

commentary.text: Verses 1–10 The temple is called the house of the Lord, because it was directed and modelled by him, and was to be employed in his service. This gave it the beauty of holiness, that it was the house of the Lord, which was far beyond all other beauties. It was to be the temple of the God of peace, therefore no iron tool must be heard; quietness and silence suit and help religious exercises. God's work should be done with much care and little noise. Clamour and violence often hinder, but never further the work of God. Thus the kingdom of God in the heart of man grows up in silence, Mr 5:27.

None employ themselves for God, without having his eye upon them. But God plainly let Solomon know that all the charge for building this temple, would neither excuse from obedience to the law of God, nor shelter from his judgments, in case of disobedience.

See what was typified by this temple. 1. Christ is the true Temple. In him dwells all the fulness of the Godhead; in him meet all God's spiritual Israel; through him we have access with confidence to God. 2. Every believer is a living temple, in whom the Spirit of God dwells, 1Co 3:16. This living temple is built upon Christ as its Foundation, and will be perfect in due time. 3. The gospel church is the mystical temple. It grows to a holy temple in the Lord, enriched and beautified with the gifts and graces of the Spirit. This temple is built firm, upon a Rock. 4. Heaven is the everlasting temple. There the church will be fixed. All that shall be stones in that building, must, in the present state of preparation, be fitted and made ready for it. Let sinners come to Jesus as the living Foundation, that they may be built on him, a part of this spiritual house, consecrated in body and soul to the glory of God.
